result:
The new title becomes searchable through an awaited event handler after the ordinary issue write. Search reads a separate SQLite copy of the content.

At server startup, `register()` in `src/instrumentation.ts` calls `registerEventHandlers()` in `src/server/services/event-registry.ts`. That function registers listeners once, including `registerSearchListeners()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`.

For a title edit, `updateIssueAction()` in `src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts` runs through `withAction()` in `src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts`, which validates the input and resolves the authenticated `Actor`. The action checks update permission, then calls `updateIssue()` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts`. The service checks organization scope, loads the existing issue, checks permission against that issue, and rejects archived issues. It then calls the repository’s `updateIssue()` in `src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts`, which updates the supplied fields and `updatedAt`, scoped by organization and issue ID.

After that write succeeds, the service awaits `emit("issue.updated", …)`. `emit()` in `src/lib/event-bus.ts` runs subscribers and waits for all of them to settle. The search listener re-reads the saved issue with `findIssueById()`, then calls `indexIssue()` and finally `upsertSearchDocument()` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts`. Thus, on the successful path, the searchable title is updated before the edit action returns. Cache revalidation follows, but the event handler is what updates search.

The copy is the `search_index` table, defined as `searchIndex` in `src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts`, with TypeScript row type `SearchIndexRow`. Each document stores its own ID, organization ID, subject kind, subject ID, nullable project ID, content, and indexing timestamp. `indexIssue()` stores `title + "\n" + description`; `indexProject()` stores name and description and uses the project’s own ID as `projectId`; `indexComment()` stores the body with a null project ID. `upsertSearchDocument()` looks up the organization/kind/subject combination, updating its content and timestamp if present or inserting a document otherwise.

`registerSearchListeners()` also indexes issue, comment, and project creation; removes documents for issue/project archival and comment deletion; and handles `search.reindex_requested` for issues. There are limits to this synchronization: event-handler failures are reported but never fail the ordinary write, and `updateComment()` and `updateProject()` do not emit indexing events. `runSearchReindexJob()` in `src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts` re-upserts projects, issues, and comments as a repair mechanism, although its implementation only fetches the first 100 of each listing rather than following subsequent cursors.

Queries have three server entry paths:

- `searchAction()` in `src/actions/search/search.ts` uses `withAction()` to validate and authenticate, checks `org:read`, loads the organization and flag context, adjusts requested kinds, and calls the search service. It returns an `ActionResult<SearchHit[]>`.
- `GET()` in `src/app/api/search/route.ts` requires `orgSlug` and `q`, resolves the actor, checks `org:read` and `command_palette`, validates a query with a limit of 10, then calls the service. It returns JSON containing `items` and `total`; errors go through `errorResponse()`.
- `Page()` in `src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx` loads tenant context, validates the URL query with a limit of 30, calls the service directly, and renders the returned hits.

`searchQuerySchema` in `src/schemas/search.ts` produces `SearchQueryInput`: an organization ID, a 1–200-character query, kinds defaulting to `["issue"]`, an optional project ID, and pagination fields. The shared schemas in `src/schemas/common.ts` require ULID-shaped IDs and an integer limit from 1 to 100.

The reusable `SearchDialog()` in `src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx` debounces input and calls its supplied `onSearch` callback. Before that call, `parseSearchQuery()` in `src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts` extracts advanced `kind:`/`in:` and `project:` tokens into filters, leaving free text in `q`; unknown tokens are omitted and described to the user. The API route and full-page search do not invoke that parser themselves.

Every server path reaches `search()` in `src/server/services/search-service.ts`, which performs checks in this order: `assertOrgScope()`, `assertCan(actor, "issue:read", …)`, `consumeRateLimit()`, organization lookup, and `advanced_search` evaluation. A schema-valid query can therefore still be refused because the actor lacks access, the organization-wide `search:query` token bucket is exhausted, or **`q` contains any colon while advanced search is disabled**. That last check includes ordinary text such as `Release: October`, not just recognized field syntax. The rate-limit token is consumed before the colon check. The actual flag definition in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` requires enterprise, with an organization override permitted.

Without advanced search, the API and page request only issues; the action filters requested kinds to issues. One implementation edge case matters: if that filtering leaves an empty array, the repository interprets it as no kind restriction.

Finally, `searchDocuments()` in `src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts` queries the copied content using SQL `LIKE '%q%'`, always filtering by organization and optionally by kind and project. It counts matching documents, applies cursor pagination, orders by `indexedAt` and document ID descending, and fetches one extra row. `keysetPredicate()`, `probeLimit()`, and `toPage()` in `src/server/repositories/_paging.ts` turn those rows into a `Page<SearchIndexRow>`; an undecodable cursor restarts from the first page.

The service maps each row into a `SearchHit`: subject kind and ID, the first content line as title, a snippet from `snippetAround()`, and a link from `hrefFor()`. It preserves the total and next cursor, then the entry point returns or renders those results.
